title: Ampullary Adenocarcinoma
subtitle: Histologic Subtypes (Pancreatobiliary vs Intestinal) and Stage-Adapted Management
provenanceNote: Clinical algorithms extracted from NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 for Ampullary Adenocarcinoma.
sourceNote: NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 - Ampullary Adenocarcinoma (AMP-1 to AMP-7, AMP-A to AMP-E)

footnotes.fn_histology: Ampullary systemic therapy is strictly stratified by histologic subtype: pancreatobiliary/mixed type follows biliary regimens (Gem-Cis, FOLFIRINOX); intestinal type follows colorectal regimens (FOLFOX, CAPOX).

nodes.name: Clinical Presentation
nodes.title: Ampullary Neoplasm: Clinical Presentation & Suspicion
nodes.description: Patients presenting with painless jaundice, biliary ductal dilation, unexplained pancreatitis, or an incidental mass at the ampulla of Vater.
bullets: Clinical presentation: fluctuating or progressive obstructive jaundice, pruritus, pale stools, dark urine, or unexplained weight loss.
Incidental detection: duodenal/ampullary prominence on screening endoscopy or biliary/pancreatic ductal dilation ('double-duct sign') on abdominal ultrasound/CT.

options.label: Suspicion of ampullary neoplasm - Proceed to diagnostic workup

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Ampullary Neoplasm: Imaging, Endoscopy, and Biomarker Checklist
nodes.description: High-quality thin-cut cross-sectional imaging, endoscopic ultrasound, and biomarker testing prior to intervention.
bullets: Pancreatic protocol MDCT (abdomen and pelvis): multi-detector dual-phase CT (pancreatic parenchymal and portal venous phases) with thin submillimeter axial sections; multiplanar reconstructions to assess vascular abutment (superior mesenteric vein/artery, celiac axis, hepatic artery).
MRI/MRCP: Alternative or problem-solving tool for characterizing CT-indeterminate liver lesions, ductal anatomy, or if severe iodinated contrast allergy.
Upper endoscopy: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) with a side-viewing duodenoscope +/- endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) with fine-needle aspiration/biopsy (FNA/FNB).
Screening colonoscopy: Recommended if not previously performed according to established age-based guidelines.
Laboratory evaluation: Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel (total/direct bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, AST, ALT), baseline CA 19-9, and CEA.

Principles of Stent Management: Preoperative biliary stenting is NOT routinely recommended prior to planned surgery due to increased risk of postoperative wound infection and complications; stent placement should be reserved ONLY for patients with acute suppurative cholangitis, severe intractable pruritus, or prolonged delay before surgery.

Germline Genetic Testing: Recommended for all patients with confirmed ampullary adenocarcinoma or positive family history of cancer, utilizing comprehensive multigene panels (ATM, BRCA1, BRCA2, CDKN2A, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PALB2, PMS2, STK11, TP53).
Tumor Biomarker Profiling: Mandatory NGS testing for mismatch repair/microsatellite instability (MMR/MSI), HER2 amplification, KRAS, BRAF V600E, NTRK gene fusions, and RET fusions.

nodes.name: Histopathology
nodes.title: Ampullary Neoplasm: Histopathologic Classification
nodes.description: Biopsy review distinguishes benign adenoma from invasive adenocarcinoma.
bullets: Ampullary adenoma: Benign glandular neoplasm with low-grade or high-grade dysplasia, without invasion through the muscularis mucosae.
Ampullary adenocarcinoma: Invasive malignant neoplasm infiltrating the submucosa, sphincter of Oddi, duodenal muscularis propria, or pancreatic parenchyma.

options.label: Benign Ampullary Adenoma (Low-grade or High-grade Dysplasia)

nodes.name: Adenoma Resection
nodes.title: Ampullary Adenoma: Endoscopic / Surgical Resection & Surveillance
nodes.description: Curative local excision for benign ampullary adenomas.
bullets: Endoscopic papillectomy / ampullectomy (Preferred): Complete en bloc or piecemeal endoscopic resection at a tertiary high-volume center; place temporary prophylactic pancreatic duct stent to prevent post-procedure pancreatitis.
Negative margins on pathology: Enter endoscopic surveillance (duodenoscopy with biopsy at 3, 6, and 12 months, then annually for up to 5 years).
Positive margins or residual adenoma: Repeat endoscopic re-excision if technically feasible, or proceed to surgical ampullectomy / transduodenal resection.
Unresectable endoscopically (large size >3-4 cm, intraductal extension >1 cm, or suspicion of occult invasion): Pancreatoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) or transduodenal surgical ampullectomy.

nodes.name: Clinical Staging
nodes.title: Invasive Ampullary Adenocarcinoma: Clinical Staging & Resectability
nodes.description: Multidisciplinary determination of resectability based on MDCT imaging and metastatic survey.
bullets: Multidisciplinary tumor board evaluation at high-volume hepatobiliary center (institutions performing >=15-20 pancreaticoduodenectomies annually).

Resectable: No distant metastases, no tumor abutment/encasement of the superior mesenteric artery (SMA), celiac axis, or common hepatic artery, and clear superior mesenteric vein (SMV)-portal vein confluence.
Borderline Resectable / High-Risk: Abutment of SMV/portal vein suitable for reconstruction, borderline arterial proximity, or markedly elevated CA 19-9.
Locally Advanced / Unresectable: Encasement (>180 degrees) of SMA or celiac axis, or unreconstructible SMV/portal vein occlusion.
Metastatic: Distant metastases (liver, peritoneum, lungs, distant retroperitoneal lymph nodes).

nodes.name: Surgical Resection
nodes.title: Resectable Ampullary Adenocarcinoma: Upfront Surgical Resection
nodes.description: Standard oncologic resection with regional lymphadenectomy.
bullets: Standard Pancreatoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure): En bloc resection of pancreatic head, duodenum, distal bile duct, and gallbladder, with regional lymphadenectomy (examination of >=12-15 lymph nodes).
Pylorus-preserving or classic Whipple: Both are acceptable oncologic approaches depending on anatomical and surgical factors.

Pathology synoptic reporting: Record primary tumor depth (pT1-pT4), nodal status (pN0-pN2), surgical margin status (R0 vs R1), lymphovascular/perineural invasion, and histological subtype (intestinal-type vs pancreatobiliary-type).

options.label: Surgery completed - Review pathologic stage and histologic subtype for adjuvant therapy

nodes.name: Adjuvant Stratification
nodes.title: Resected Ampullary Cancer: Pathologic Stage & Histologic Subtype
nodes.description: Adjuvant systemic therapy is determined by pathologic stage (Stage I vs Stage II/III) and histologic phenotype (pancreatobiliary vs intestinal).
bullets: Stage I (pT1 N0 M0): Highly favorable prognosis; observe or consider single-agent adjuvant therapy.
Stage II/III (pT2-T4 or pN+ M0): Adjuvant systemic chemotherapy for up to 6 months is standard.
Histologic subtyping (ESPAC-3 / NCCN):
• Pancreatobiliary/Mixed type: Infiltrating simple glands/cords with desmoplastic stroma; treated with gemcitabine/cisplatin or modified FOLFIRINOX.
• Intestinal type: Cribriform or tubular glands resembling colorectal adenocarcinoma; treated with fluorouracil/oxaliplatin (mFOLFOX6 or CAPOX).

options.label: Pathologic Stage I (pT1 N0 M0) - Any Histology
Pathologic Stage II / III - Pancreatobiliary or Mixed Subtype
Pathologic Stage II / III - Intestinal Subtype

nodes.name: Stage I Adjuvant
nodes.title: Stage I (pT1 N0): Observation or Adjuvant Chemotherapy
nodes.description: Management for early resected ampullary cancer.
bullets: Observation (Preferred option for selected T1aN0 tumors with R0 resection and no lymphovascular invasion).
Adjuvant Systemic Therapy: In patients with adverse features (high histologic grade, perineural invasion), consider 6 months of:
• Capecitabine monotherapy (1250 mg/m2 PO BID days 1-14 q21d), OR
• Gemcitabine monotherapy (1000 mg/m2 IV days 1, 8, 15 q28d) based on ESPAC-3 trial.
Post-treatment surveillance: Regular clinical visits, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, and tumor markers (CA 19-9, CEA) every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months for up to 5 years.

nodes.name: Adj Pancreatobiliary Tx
nodes.title: Stage II/III Pancreatobiliary Ampullary Cancer: Adjuvant Chemotherapy
nodes.description: Adjuvant systemic regimens for pancreatobiliary/mixed ampullary adenocarcinoma.
bullets: Preferred Adjuvant Regimens (Up to 6 months total duration):
• Gemcitabine + Cisplatin (gi-ampullary): Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 + Cisplatin 25 mg/m2 IV days 1 & 8 every 21 days for up to 8 cycles. Established biliary/ampullary standard.

• Modified FOLFIRINOX (folfirinox): Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150-180 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, 5-FU 2400 mg/m2 46-h continuous infusion q14d x 12 cycles (in young, fit patients with ECOG 0-1).
• Gemcitabine + Capecitabine (GemCap): Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 days 1, 8, 15 q28d + Capecitabine 1660 mg/m2/day days 1-21 q28d (ESPAC-4 inspired).
• Gemcitabine monotherapy: 1000 mg/m2 days 1, 8, 15 q28d x 6 cycles (for patients unfit for doublet therapy).
Chemoradiation: May be considered for positive surgical margins (R1 resection) or extensive nodal involvement.
Surveillance: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast and CA 19-9 every 3 months for year 1-2, then every 6 months.

nodes.name: Adj Intestinal Tx
nodes.title: Stage II/III Intestinal Ampullary Cancer: Adjuvant Chemotherapy
nodes.description: Adjuvant systemic regimens for intestinal-type ampullary adenocarcinoma.
bullets: Preferred Adjuvant Regimens (Colorectal-inspired systemic therapy x 6 months):
• Modified FOLFOX6 (modified-folfox-6): Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, 5-FU bolus 400 mg/m2 then 2400 mg/m2 46-h continuous infusion every 14 days for 12 cycles.
• CAPOX: Capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 PO BID days 1-14 + Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 IV day 1 every 21 days for 8 cycles.
• Capecitabine or 5-FU/leucovorin monotherapy: Acceptable options if oxaliplatin-ineligible or for low-risk Stage II disease.
Surveillance: H&P, chest/abdomen/pelvis CT with IV contrast, and CEA/CA 19-9 every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months for up to 5 years.

nodes.name: Borderline Neoadjuvant
nodes.title: Borderline Resectable Ampullary Cancer: Neoadjuvant Therapy
nodes.description: Preoperative systemic therapy and restaging for high-risk or borderline resectable disease.
bullets: Neoadjuvant Systemic Therapy (2-4 months):
• Pancreatobiliary/Mixed: Modified FOLFIRINOX (folfirinox) or Gemcitabine + Cisplatin (gi-ampullary) or Gemcitabine + Nab-paclitaxel.
• Intestinal Subtype: Modified FOLFOX6 or CAPOX.
Consider Neoadjuvant Chemoradiation: 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent capecitabine or fluorouracil following induction chemotherapy if vascular margins remain close.
Restaging: High-resolution pancreatic protocol MDCT after 2-4 months of therapy. If stable or regression with no distant metastases, proceed to exploratory laparotomy and pancreatoduodenectomy.

nodes.name: Locally Advanced Tx
nodes.title: Unresectable Locally Advanced Ampullary Cancer: Definitive Therapy
nodes.description: Definitive systemic chemotherapy and chemoradiation for locally advanced disease.
bullets: Biliary drainage: Ensure adequate biliary decompression with permanent self-expanding metal stent (SEMS) prior to systemic therapy.
First-line Systemic Therapy: Administer full-dose combination systemic chemotherapy based on histologic subtype (Gem-Cis or mFOLFIRINOX for pancreatobiliary; mFOLFOX6 for intestinal).

Consolidative Chemoradiation: For patients with disease control (absence of progression) after 4-6 months of chemotherapy, consolidative chemoradiation (capecitabine or 5-FU concurrent with 50.4 Gy IMRT) may provide durable local control and symptom palliation.
Re-evaluate for resectability: In rare cases of dramatic tumor shrinkage, restage and discuss surgical exploration.

nodes.name: Metastatic Subtype
nodes.title: Metastatic Ampullary Cancer: Histologic & Molecular Stratification
nodes.description: Systemic therapy for metastatic ampullary cancer is strictly bifurcated by histologic subtype and molecular drivers.
bullets: Pancreatobiliary/Mixed: Managed according to NCCN Biliary Tract / Pancreatic Cancer guidelines.
Intestinal: Managed according to NCCN Colorectal / Small Bowel Cancer guidelines.
Mandatory molecular testing: MSI/dMMR, HER2, BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, NTRK fusions, and RET fusions.

nodes.name: Met Pancreatobiliary Tx
nodes.title: Metastatic Pancreatobiliary Ampullary Cancer: Systemic & Targeted Regimens
nodes.description: First-line chemotherapy backbones and biomarker-directed targeted agents.
bullets: Preferred First-Line Cytotoxic Regimens:
• Gemcitabine + Cisplatin (gi-ampullary): Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 + Cisplatin 25 mg/m2 IV days 1 & 8 every 21 days (can add Durvalumab or Pembrolizumab per biliary standards).
• Modified FOLFIRINOX (folfirinox): For patients with ECOG PS 0-1 and preserved hepatic function/bilirubin <1.5x ULN.
• Gemcitabine + Nab-paclitaxel: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 + Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 IV days 1, 8, 15 every 28 days.
Biomarker-Directed Targeted Therapy:
• MSI-H / dMMR: Pembrolizumab (200 mg q3w or 400 mg q6w) or Dostarlimab (preferred first-line or subsequent).
• NTRK gene fusion: Larotrectinib or Entrectinib.
• RET gene fusion: Selpercatinib.
• BRAF V600E mutation: Dabrafenib + Trametinib.
• KRAS G12C mutation: Sotorasib or Adagrasib (subsequent therapy).
Supportive care: Palliative biliary stent patency monitoring, analgesia, and nutritional counseling.

nodes.name: Met Intestinal Tx
nodes.title: Metastatic Intestinal Ampullary Cancer: Systemic & Targeted Regimens
nodes.description: First-line colorectal-aligned systemic and targeted regimens.
bullets: Preferred First-Line Cytotoxic Regimens:
• Modified FOLFOX6 (modified-folfox-6): Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, 5-FU bolus + 2400 mg/m2 continuous infusion q14d (+/- bevacizumab).
• CAPOX: Capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 PO BID x 14d + Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 day 1 q21d (+/- bevacizumab).
• FOLFIRI (folfiri): Irinotecan 180 mg/m2, leucovorin, 5-FU continuous infusion (+/- bevacizumab).
Biomarker-Directed Targeted Therapy:
• MSI-H / dMMR: Pembrolizumab (preferred first-line) or Nivolumab +/- Ipilimumab.
• HER2 Amplified (RAS wild-type): Trastuzumab + Pertuzumab or Trastuzumab + Tucatinib.
• BRAF V600E mutation: Encorafenib + Cetuximab (subsequent therapy).
• NTRK / RET / KRAS G12C: Larotrectinib, Selpercatinib, or Sotorasib/Adagrasib respectively.

Oligometastatic disease: For patients with solitary liver or lung metastases achieving prolonged disease control on systemic therapy, consider surgical resection or stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT).
